{{short description|Indonesian entrepreneur and scientist (born 1975)}}'''Roby Muhamad''' is an Indonesian entrepreneur and scientist best known for his work with social network dynamics.<ref name=acer>Ketut Krisna Wijaya, [https://www.techinasia.com/ceo-left-acer-build-social-network-indonesia-raised-3m This CEO left Acer to build a social network in Indonesia, and just raised $3M]. Tech In Asia, 1 September 2015. Accessed 25 June 2018.</ref> His work spans the fields of [[physics]], [[psychology]], and [[sociology]].

Muhamad earned his bachelor in physics from the [[Bandung Institute of Technology]],<ref name=convo>[https://theconversation.com/profiles/roby-muhamad-337231 Roby Muhamad]. [[The Conversation (website)|The Conversation]], accessed 25 June 2018.</ref> and he earned his doctorate in sociology from [[Columbia University]].<ref name=acer/><ref name=date>Nadine Frieschild, [https://www.techinasia.com/investors-dont-love-dating-apps-raised-3m-series Investors don’t love dating apps? This one just raised a $3M series A round]. Tech In Asia, 12 August 2015. Accessed 25 June 2018.</ref> He current lectures at the Department of Psychology at the [[University of Indonesia]].<ref name=convo/> In 2003, Muhamad and [[Duncan J. Watts]] were part of the team which roughly confirmed [[Stanley Milgram]]'s hypothesis on [[six degrees of separation]].<ref>Stefanie Knoll and John Wihbey, [https://journalistsresource.org/studies/international/globalization/small-worlds-clash-civilizations-new-data-dimensions-globalized-world Small worlds and the clash of civilizations: New data on the dimensions of a globalized world]. [[Journalist's Resource]], 28 July 2015. Accessed 25 June 2018.</ref>

Muhamad is co-owner of the location-based dating app Yogurt.<ref name=acer/><ref name=convo/><ref name=date/> He has made public calls for modernizing anti-tobacco efforts targeted at teenagers due to tobacco companies use of social media to negate teens' rational calculation of loss-benefit.<ref>Elly Burhaini Faizal, [http://www.thejakartapost.com/news/2016/03/21/social-media-plays-role-youth-smoking-says-expert.html Social media plays role in youth smoking, says expert]. [[Jakarta Post]], 21 March 2016. Accessed 25 July 2019</ref>
